summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old female was admitted for increased total body edema and concern for possible cellulitis in the left lower extremity. The swelling was attributed to chronic lymphedema, venous insufficiency, and obesity, with no evidence of heart failure, kidney injury, or liver disease. A low-dose Lasix trial improved facial and hand swelling, but the medication was not continued at discharge due to prior renal risks. Persistent erythema in the left leg prompted a short course of clindamycin. Her INR remained therapeutic on warfarin, phenytoin levels were normal, and sleep apnea was noted for outpatient follow-up. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to elevate her legs, wear compression stockings, and follow up with her primary care provider regarding diuretic management and further evaluation.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of other female genital organs
